entries.name: 干支・子（ねずみ）
entries.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Create ONE photorealistic full-body transparent cutout of elderly Japanese Kozo in a charming animal mascot kigurumi costume for a twelve-animal Japanese zodiac series. Reference image 1 is his IDENTITY: keep EXACT recognizable elderly wrinkled smiling face, age, gray hair and natural elderly build. Reference image 2 is ONLY the production style reference for the plush full-body costume, face opening and studio photography, NOT its rabbit species. Replace all original clothes and fishing cap with the specified costume. His real human face is clearly visible in a large oval opening in the FRONT of the animal head hood, surrounded by plush fabric; animal eyes, snout and ears sit ABOVE and BESIDE the face opening, never across his eyes or mouth. Maintain the same Kozo face and cheerful gentle smile. A complete premium soft plush mascot suit from hood to oversized matching plush animal feet, rounded padded belly, believable fabric seams, fluffy detailed material, charming cute proportions. The arms end in simple soft padded animal paw mittens appropriate to the species. Do not show human fingers protruding from paws. One coherent wearable costume, not an actual live animal or a face replaced by animal. Single person, standing, full body including the entire hood, all ears, horns, paws, feet and full tail completely framed with generous transparent padding at least 35 pixels on all sides. Slight three-quarter frontal view so the tail can be visible beside or behind body. True alpha transparency in background and gaps; no backdrop, no glow, no fake checkerboard, no gradient, no scenery, no floor plane. Soft neutral photographic studio lighting, natural textures. No hats from reference, no accessories unrelated to the animal, no text, zodiac lettering, logos, watermarks, existing franchise designs or additional characters. The result is a photographic cutout for compositing beside the user's photo.

One paw raised in a friendly wave, other paw resting near belly. Do not use rabbit ears.
